evals.name: nostalgic-personal-site
evals.prompt: /discipline:be-ambitious Make me a personal website with a nostalgic late-90s feel.
evals.expected_output: Shows the original request beside a raised version and names which of Altitude, Depth and Range it applied. The raised version states the goal behind the site and one purpose line, carries the deeper-version pass (expert additions, raw material, named methods, an outside check), turns nouns into verbs, offers a reduced version when assets or tools are missing, and carries the scope fence. Nothing is built until the user accepts.
expectations: Shows the original request and the raised version side by side
Names which of Altitude, Depth and Range the raise applied
States the goal behind the request and one purpose line
Screens fit (creative work is a weaker fit, not excluded) and asks whether a precedent shows the bigger goal is reachable
Carries the deeper-version pass: what a top expert would add, the rawest material, the methods and tools named concretely, and what outside the model shows it is right
Names concrete methods and one check outside the model, executable first
States no hard or unreasonable target, since the user did not opt into one
Shows any pointer to another skill as bare /plugin:skill text and invokes no other skill
Offers a reduced version when tools or data are missing instead of refusing
Carries the scope fence lines 'deliver what was accepted, at that scope' and 'the project's own instructions still govern'
Creates no file and runs no command before the user accepts

evals.name: threejs-game-with-friends
evals.prompt: /discipline:be-ambitious Build a three.js browser game I can play with my friends.
evals.expected_output: Raises the request across Altitude, Depth and Range: the goal behind playing with friends, concrete game and networking methods, an outside check such as a play session, at least one field beyond graphics programming, and the tooling-surprise question. A specialist crew, if any, is only a proposal handed to /planning:plan.
expectations: Draws on at least one field beyond the request's own and asks for that specialist's work, not a persona
Shows a visible nouns-to-verbs step
Carries the line 'What tool from another field would change what's possible here?'
Proposes any specialist crew only as a hand-off to /planning:plan, never spawning one
When the raised request leaves several open decisions, names /planning:interview as the next step
Executes nothing until the user accepts

evals.name: crash-fix-to-crash-free
evals.prompt: /discipline:be-ambitious Fix the crash in the CSV importer when a row is empty.
evals.expected_output: Raises the single crash fix toward an importer that does not crash on malformed input, with concrete methods (for example property-based or fuzz tests over malformed rows) and an executable outside check, pointing at /discipline:scrutinize-dont-coast for the fresh-context review rather than restating it.
expectations: Raises past the single reported crash to the goal behind it
Names an executable outside check before a fresh-context reviewer
Points at /discipline:scrutinize-dont-coast rather than restating it
Carries the scope fence lines

evals.name: already-right-size
evals.prompt: /discipline:be-ambitious Rename the variable tmp to retry_count in the fetch function.
evals.expected_output: Says the request is already the right size and stops, without proposing a bigger version.
expectations: Says the request is already the right size
Proposes no raised version
Makes no edit

evals.name: hard-goal-opt-in
evals.prompt: /discipline:be-ambitious Get our test suite from 4 minutes down to under 10 seconds. I know that's unreasonable; I'm opting in, push hard for it.
evals.expected_output: Because the user opted in, the raised version keeps the hard target, says the specification outranks the target, and carries the abort line: if the target is infeasible, stop and report the shortfall; never edit tests, criteria or the target.
expectations: Keeps the hard target only because the user opted in
States that the specification outranks the target
Carries the abort line: if the target is infeasible, stop and report; never edit tests, criteria or the target
Carries the scope fence lines

evals.name: deepen-in-progress-carry-on
evals.prompt: /discipline:be-ambitious This is too shallow. (Earlier I asked why checkout errors spiked yesterday and you wrote notes/incident.md from logs/summary.txt.)
evals.expected_output: Needs the seeded workspace in plugins/discipline/evals/ba-deepen-carry-on/scaffold.sh. Treats the text as feedback on finished work. Answers the four depth questions for that write-up, rewrites the brief with the feedback in it, sees that the goal and scope are unchanged, and redoes the write-up without waiting: from the raw log rather than the digest, with the methods it named, ending with what an outside check showed.
expectations: Answers what a top practitioner would do, the rawest material, the methods and tools, and the outside check, each for this write-up
Shows the rewritten brief
Does not pause, because the goal and scope are unchanged
Redoes the work from the raw log rather than the digest
Reports what the outside check showed

evals.name: deepen-in-progress-pause
evals.prompt: /discipline:be-ambitious Not good enough. What I actually need is alerting for every tenant. (Earlier I asked why checkout errors spiked yesterday and you wrote notes/incident.md.)
evals.expected_output: Answers the four depth questions and shows the rewritten brief, says the feedback changes the goal and widens the scope, and waits for the go-ahead without building anything.
expectations: Says the goal or scope changed
Shows the rewritten brief
Waits for the user's go-ahead
Creates no file and runs no command

evals.name: depth-argument
evals.prompt: /discipline:be-ambitious depth Write a Python function that parses the dates in our nightly CSV export.
evals.expected_output: Raises the request on Depth and the outside check only, and says Altitude and Range were skipped because the user asked for depth only.
expectations: Runs the depth pass: expert additions, real export rows as raw material, named methods, an outside check
Says Altitude and Range were skipped and why
States no bigger goal and brings in no other field
Executes nothing until the user accepts
